subject.title: Apply design-system composer to app chat UI

question: Should the composer redesign land together with the new Settings section while retaining the restored inline speaker control, or should these UX changes be narrowed into separate PRs?
rationale: The branch combines a broad composer redesign, shared flyout behavior, a persisted tool-call option, and two speech-control surfaces; automated checks cannot determine the intended permanent UX ownership.

options.title: Narrow and split
options.body: Land the composer restyle separately from Settings ownership changes so each UX decision can be independently reviewed and proven.

options.title: Approve combined UX
options.body: Keep the combined composer and Settings changes, explicitly accepting the inline and Settings speech controls after current-head proof.

options.title: Wait for design seed
options.body: Pause until the direction of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/962 is settled, then align the implementation with that decision.

recommendation.title: Narrow and split
recommendation.body: Land the composer restyle separately from Settings ownership changes so each UX decision can be independently reviewed and proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the same composer interaction surface provides the strongest available routing signal for this UX decision.
